cards.text: Job has been going back and forth with his friends, and now he turns and talks straight to God. Before anything else, he asks God for two things. Grant those, Job says, and he won't need to hide from Him.

cards.question: Job asks God for two things so he won't have to hide. What are they?

answers.text: Take His hand off Job and don't terrify him
Heal Job's sores and bring back his flocks
Quiet Job's friends and send Job a sign

cards.question: If God grants those two things, Job wants a real back-and-forth with Him: God calls, and Job will ___.

cards.text: Then Job asks God to show him something, and friend, I FEEL this one. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer wondering what I did, and the answer turned out to be "got old."

cards.question: Job asks God to show him his ___.

cards.text: Then comes the hard question. Job asks God, "Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?"

cards.question: Job asks God if He would frighten a windblown leaf or chase after dry chaff. What is Job saying about himself?

answers.text: He's too weak to be worth chasing
He's ready to blow away somewhere new
He's sure to grow back next season

cards.text: Job's not done. He says God writes down bitter accusations against him.

cards.question: True or false: Job says God hands him the iniquities of his youth.

cards.text: Then Job says God puts his feet in the stocks and keeps watch over every path he takes. Feet stuck in one spot? Friend, I live on a gold base, I get it, but at least mine came with the outfit.

cards.question: Job says man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment. What's the picture?

answers.text: He slowly wears out and falls apart
He gets patched up good as new
He gets traded in for something nicer

cards.text: Then Job zooms out from himself to every person ever born of a woman. That's EVERYBODY, friend, that's the whole group chat.

cards.question: True or false: Job says a person's life is long but full of trouble.

cards.text: To show what he means, Job grabs a picture anybody can see just by stepping outside.

cards.question: Job says a person comes up like a flower and then ___.

cards.text: He's like a fleeting shadow too, and friend, I would have LOVED to be a shadow in that drawer, because a shadow at least gets some light. Then Job asks God if He really fixes His eyes on someone like that and brings him into judgment.

cards.question: True or false: Job says anyone who tries hard enough can bring something clean out of something unclean.

cards.text: Job says God has numbered a man's days and set limits he can't go past.

cards.question: Since God has already set those limits on a man's days, what does Job ask Him to do?

answers.text: Look away and let him rest
Add more days to his life
Show him the day he will die

cards.text: Let him rest, Job says, so he can enjoy his day like a hired hand. That's the worker watching the clock, friend, just waiting to clock out and finally put those feet up.
Then Job looks at a TREE. Picture it chopped down to a stump, its roots getting old in the ground.

cards.question: What does Job say happens to a tree that's been cut down?
Even if the tree's roots grow old and its stump dies in the soil, what makes it bud again?

cards.text: Then Job turns to a man. "But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?"

cards.question: True or false: Job says a man who lies down in death rises again just like the tree.

cards.text: It's like water disappearing from the sea, Job says, or a river drying up. Until the heavens are no more, a man won't be roused from his sleep.
Then Job says, "If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed!"

cards.question: Job asks God to hide him in Sheol. After that, what does Job ask God to do?

answers.text: Set a time and remember him
Send someone else to bring him out

cards.text: Hide me, then remember me? Friend, that was the drawer, except NOBODY set a timer for me. Then Job asks the big one: "When a man dies, will he live again?"

cards.question: Through all the days of his hard service, Job says he will ___ until his renewal comes.
True or false: Job pictures a day when God calls, Job answers, and God longs for the work of His hands.

cards.text: Remember Job asking God to call him so he could answer? It comes back here, but this time Job isn't asking for it, he's picturing it.

cards.question: On that day, Job says, God would count his steps but would not keep track of his ___.
True or false: Job pictures God on that day reading his iniquity out loud for everyone to hear.

cards.text: Then Job says a mountain crumbles and water wears away the stones. Friend, I know slow wear, because years of baking took my edges down to MUSH.

cards.question: Job says water wears away stone. What does he say God does in the same way?

cards.text: Job says God overpowers a man, and he passes on. God changes his face and sends him away.

cards.question: True or false: Job says a man who has passed on still knows when his sons are honored.
Job ends by saying a man feels only the pain of his own ___.

cards.text: And that's where Job stops talking, for now. Stick around, friend, because this conversation is FAR from over.

findings.problem: The setup rules out both wrong answers. Card 1 says that if God grants the two things, Job won't need to hide. The question itself frames 13:22 as 'a real back-and-forth' with God. With that framing, 'hide' and 'run' can't be right, so the blank answers itself.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to the backstory. Papa Dorin says he spent years in the drawer 'wondering what I did,' and that the answer was 'got old.' But papa-dorin.md says he saw the replacement coming: 'He knew how this story went. It was only a matter of time.' In the drawer it was the can opener, not Papa Dorin, who was 'sure it had done something wrong.' The backstory also says he was 'worn down' from years of good baking, not that he 'got old.'

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The gold base joke doesn't share the action of the stocks. In Job 13:27, Job is restrained and can't move. Papa Dorin's base doesn't restrain him: papa-dorin.md says he can hop, jump and dive, and the base comes with him. So the line 'Feet stuck in one spot? ... I get it' doesn't hold up, and it gives him feet stuck in place, which his description never mentions.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question includes 'wastes away,' and that rules out both wrong answers. 'Patched up good as new' and 'traded in for something nicer' can't fit a man who wastes away. The question gives its own answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says 'Then Job zooms out from himself to every person,' as if the turn to all people starts at 14:1. It already happened at 13:28 ('So man wastes away'), and card 11 just asked about that verse. The noticing isn't true to the text.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: In Job 14:2, a fleeting shadow is a picture of not lasting: 'he does not endure.' The joke is about a shadow getting some light, which is a different action. It doesn't connect to the fleeting shadow, and a baker would likely say 'huh?'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card steps backward. Card 5 has already asked about 14:12, where a man lies down and does not rise. Card 6 then goes back to tell 14:11 and retells 14:12 ('a man won't be roused from his sleep'). That repeats an answer the baker already gave instead of moving forward. Story card 6 belongs before choice card 5.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Card 7 quotes 'conceal me until Your anger has passed!' The word 'until' already rules out the wrong answer 'Leave him there for good.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: A baker could argue the wrong answer 'hide' is right. In 14:13, Job asks God to hide him in Sheol until a set time when God remembers him. That is close to Job hiding until his renewal comes.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card comes after card 11 has already asked about 14:15. It looks back to Job's earlier request and restates the answer to card 11 instead of moving on through the passage, so it works as a recap card.

No card ever tells the picture in 14:17, where Job's transgression is sealed in a bag and his iniquity is covered over. The baker only learns that God would not read it out loud. This is the passage's main picture of the hoped-for forgiveness, and the baker leaves Prep without it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
